title: Compatible henselian G-ring stage for a finite etale closed-fibre cover
statement: Let (A,I) be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec} A proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and V finite etale over Y_0=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec} A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I) [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-pc-fibre-product]. There exist a commutative G-ring B [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], an ideal J with (B,J) henselian, a proper g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec} B, a morphism s:Y\to Z, a morphism k:Y_0\to Z_0=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec} B}\operatorname{Spec}(B/J), and a finite etale W\to Z_0 such that s\circ j_Y=j_Z\circ k, where j_Y and j_Z are the first projections of these closed-fibre pullbacks, and W\times_{Z_0}Y_0\cong V as Y_0-schemes. This statement asserts no finite etale lift of V to Y or of W to Z.

source.place: Tag 0GS2, proof, General case, approximation and descent before applying the G-ring lifting case; official online text https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GS2

proof.text: Noetherian approximation of $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $f$ is proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-limit-noetherian] (affine clause) there are a directed set $\Lambda$ and an inverse system $(f_\lambda:Y_\lambda\to S_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ with affine transition morphisms, $f_\lambda$ proper, $S_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}A_\lambda$ with $A_\lambda$ a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra, $Y=\varprojlim_\lambda Y_\lambda$ (projections $p_\lambda:Y\to Y_\lambda$), $\operatorname{Spec}A=\varprojlim_\lambda S_\lambda$ and $A=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda$ with coprojections $\alpha_\lambda:A_\lambda\to A$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], and $f_\lambda\circ p_\lambda=(\operatorname{Spec}\alpha_\lambda)\circ f$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'General case' (lines ~1846-1878)

proof.text: The ideals. Put $I_\lambda=\alpha_\lambda^{-1}(I)\subseteq A_\lambda$. For $\mu\le\lambda$ the transition map $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu\to A_\lambda$ satisfies $\alpha_\lambda\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\alpha_\mu$, so $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}(I_\mu)\subseteq I_\lambda$ and $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ is a directed system of pairs. Every $x\in A$ is $\alpha_\lambda(a)$ for some $\lambda$ and $a\in A_\lambda$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]; if $x\in I$ then $a\in I_\lambda$. Hence $I=\bigcup_\lambda\alpha_\lambda(I_\lambda)$, i.e. $(A,I)=\varinjlim_\lambda(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ as pairs, and the induced maps $A_\lambda/I_\lambda\to A/I$ are injective with union $A/I$, so $A/I=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda/I_\lambda$. (Stacks: 'Thus we also have $I=\colim I_i$ and $A/I=\colim A_i/I_i$'.)

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'General case' (lines ~1846-1878)

proof.text: The closed fibres form an inverse system with limit $Y_0$. Put $S_{\lambda,0}=\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\lambda)$, $Y_{\lambda,0}=Y_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}S_{\lambda,0}$ and $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. (a) By step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], $S_0=\varprojlim_\lambda S_{\lambda,0}$. (b) For $\mu\le\lambda$ the morphism $Y_{\lambda,0}\to Y_{\mu,0}$ induced by $Y_\lambda\to Y_\mu$ and $S_{\lambda,0}\to S_{\mu,0}$ factors as $Y_{\lambda,0}=Y_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\lambda)\to Y_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\mu A_\lambda)=Y_\lambda\times_{Y_\mu}Y_{\mu,0}\to Y_{\mu,0}$: the first arrow is a base change of the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\lambda)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\mu A_\lambda)$ ($I_\mu A_\lambda\subseteq I_\lambda$ by step 2), hence a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], hence affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; the second is a base change of the affine $Y_\lambda\to Y_\mu$, hence affine [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]; a composite of affine morphisms is affine (preimages of affine opens stay affine). So $(Y_{\lambda,0})$ is an inverse system with affine transition morphisms, and its limit exists [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. (c) Each $Y_{\lambda,0}\to S_{\lambda,0}$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]; as $S_{\lambda,0}$ is affine, $Y_{\lambda,0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. (d) $Y_0=\varprojlim_\lambda Y_{\lambda,0}$ with projections $q_\lambda=p_\lambda\times(S_0\to S_{\lambda,0}):Y_0\to Y_{\lambda,0}$: for every scheme $T$, $\operatorname{Mor}(T,\varprojlim Y_{\lambda,0})=\varprojlim_\lambda\big(\operatorname{Mor}(T,Y_\lambda)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}(T,S_\lambda)}\operatorname{Mor}(T,S_{\lambda,0})\big)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and since limits commute with limits this is $\operatorname{Mor}(T,Y)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}(T,\operatorname{Spec}A)}\operatorname{Mor}(T,S_0)=\operatorname{Mor}(T,Y_0)$ by step 1 and (a), naturally in $T$; conclude by Yoneda. (Stacks: 'The same thing is true for schemes finite etale over $X_0=\lim(X_i\times_{S_i}S_{i,0})$'.)

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'General case' (lines ~1846-1878)

proof.text: Descent of $V$ to a finite stage. $V\to Y_0$ is finite, hence affine, quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and etale, hence locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; so it is of finite presentation. By [thm-pd-spreading-out] (1), applied to the system $(Y_{\lambda,0})$ of step 3 (qcqs, affine transitions, limit $Y_0$), there are $\lambda_0$ and a morphism of finite presentation $V_{\lambda_0}\to Y_{\lambda_0,0}$ with $V_{\lambda_0}\times_{Y_{\lambda_0,0}}Y_0\cong V$ over $Y_0$; $V_{\lambda_0}$ is qcqs, being of finite presentation over the qcqs $Y_{\lambda_0,0}$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$ put $V_\lambda=V_{\lambda_0}\times_{Y_{\lambda_0,0}}Y_{\lambda,0}$: $V_\lambda\to Y_{\lambda,0}$ is the base change of $V_{\lambda_0}\to Y_{\lambda_0,0}$ to the stage $Y_{\lambda,0}$, and its base change to the limit $Y_0$ is $V\to Y_0$, finite and etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite] ($V_{\lambda_0}\to Y_{\lambda_0,0}$ locally of finite type) and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] (it is locally of finite presentation) there are $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge\lambda_0$ with $V_{\lambda_1}\to Y_{\lambda_1,0}$ finite and $V_{\lambda_2}\to Y_{\lambda_2,0}$ etale; for $\lambda\ge\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ ($\Lambda$ directed), $V_\lambda\to Y_{\lambda,0}$ is a base change of both, hence finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], and $V_\lambda\times_{Y_{\lambda,0}}Y_0\cong V$ over $Y_0$. Fix such a $\lambda$ from now on. (Stacks: the category of finite etale schemes over $X_0$ is the limit of those over the $X_{i,0}$, by Limits 01ZM, 01ZO, 07RP; only its essential surjectivity is used here.)

proof.text: At the chosen stage, henselize the pair (A_i,I_i) using [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Its quotient is A_i/I_i and it is henselian. The finite-type integer ring A_i is a G-ring by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-g-ring], so its henselization B is a G-ring by [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-pair-g-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-universal-property] to A_i -> A and the henselian pair (A,I): the ideal I_i maps into I by its definition. This gives beta:B -> A extending the stage map and carrying J=I_i B into I. Only this one-stage factorization is needed, not a colimit of all henselizations.

proof.text: Let Z=Y_i times Spec B over Spec A_i, with proper projection g by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The limit projection Y -> Y_i and Spec beta after f define s:Y -> Z by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The quotient isomorphism A_i/I_i -> B/J identifies Z_0 with Y_i,0, using [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. Transport the descended finite etale cover to W over Z_0. The induced quotient map B/J -> A/I and the closed-fibre projection define k:Y_0 -> Z_0. Both j_Y followed by s and k followed by j_Z project to the same maps to Y_i and Spec B: the first equality is the limit-cone relation, and the second is Spec of the equality (A -> A/I) composed with beta = (B/J -> A/I) composed with (B -> B/J). Pullback extensionality gives the required equality. Pasting the squares identifies the base change of W along k with the original descended cover pulled back to Y_0, hence with V, over Y_0. No lift over Y or Z is claimed.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtale_henselian_gRing_stage
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I]
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f]
    (V : (@IsFinite ⊓ @Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).Over ⊤
      (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : IsGRing B)
      (J : Ideal B) (_ : HenselianRing B J) (Z : Scheme.{u})
      (g : Z ⟶ Spec (.of B)) (_ : IsProper g) (s : Y ⟶ Z)
      (k : pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) ⟶
        pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J))))
      (W : (@IsFinite ⊓ @Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).Over ⊤
        (pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J))))),
      (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) ≫ s =
        k ≫ pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)))) ∧
      Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd W.hom k) ≅ Over.mk V.hom)
